chunks.content: # CLO Master Express Lesson 14: Wedding Dress Masterclass Live Stream This document details the step-by-step process and technical insights for creating a complex multi-layer wedding dress in CLO 6.1 software. It covers production logic, pattern creation, fabric physical property adjustments, sewing techniques, simulation tips, and layering methods to achieve realistic and stable garment simulation. --- ## Introduction to CLO 6.1 and Production Logic for Wedding Dresses This section introduces the CLO 6.1 software interface adjustments, virtual model setup, and the fundamental production logic for creating complex multi-layer wedding dresses using CLO. - **Software Version & Interface Setup**: - CLO 6.1 used for the live stream. - Toolbar repositioned to left and right sides with tool selection toggled off to display most tools. - Virtual model adjusted by Grace from the CLO library. - New CLO 6.1 features include model makeup and skin color adjustment. - **Production Logic**: - Wedding dresses consist of multiple layers and complex internal structures. - Production proceeds top-to-bottom, from internal support to outer layers, layer by layer. - Each layer’s simulation must be stable before proceeding to the next. - Ensures garment stability and avoids conflicts during layering. --- ## Creating the Internal Support Structure and Pattern Preparation This section details drawing the internal fishbone support structure, generating 2D patterns from 3D lines, and preparing sewing lines and flanges. - **Fishbone Structure Drawing**: - Use the 3D Pen tool on the virtual model to create the internal fishbone framework. - Add 3D dividing lines to distinguish pattern pieces. - **Flattening and Arranging Patterns**: - Use the Flatten tool to convert 3D lines into 2D patterns. - Arrange pattern pieces in the 2D window to avoid confusion. - **Pattern Editing and Cloning**: - Edit patterns and sewing lines as necessary. - Clone patterns for further manipulation. - **Flange Creation and Sewing**: - Ensure flange length and width consistency (width = 1 cm; height = length of sewing line). - Position flange on opposite side and freeze it. - Sew flange using 5mm internal sewing line between flange sides and main pattern. - Adjust flange position in 3D window for accuracy. - **Adding Fabric for Support**: - Assign physical attribute “Trim Hardware” temporarily to fishbone fabric for firmness. - Use defined physical attribute fabrics to modify support material. - Add sticky strips on top and bottom panel lines for structural support. - Freeze modifications for stability. --- ## Upper Body Dress Pattern Assembly and Sewing This section covers assembling the upper body 2D patterns, internal line creation, panel adjustments, and sewing procedures. - **Pattern Display**: - Set 2D pattern window display to “Translucent Surface” for better visualization. - **Point-to-Point Connection and Internal Lines**: - Connect number 1 pattern pieces point-to-point and assemble. - Use measurement tools to mark and hook internal lines. - Draw internal multidirectional lines to complete front and back panels. - **Panel Rearrangement**: - Add or delete panels as needed for design flexibility. - Adjust curves and closed points to ensure accurate cutting lines.

chunks.content: - **Pattern Display**: - Set 2D pattern window display to “Translucent Surface” for better visualization. - **Point-to-Point Connection and Internal Lines**: - Connect number 1 pattern pieces point-to-point and assemble. - Use measurement tools to mark and hook internal lines. - Draw internal multidirectional lines to complete front and back panels. - **Panel Rearrangement**: - Add or delete panels as needed for design flexibility. - Adjust curves and closed points to ensure accurate cutting lines. - **Sewing Panels**: - Use 1 to n free sewing tool to sew outer and inner layers together. - Change sewing thread type to “Turned” at fold areas. - Arrange and simulate the sewn upper body. - **Project Saving**: - Save project file before proceeding to next production steps to prevent data loss. --- ## Two Methods for Creating the Wedding Dress Skirt (“Group Name”) This section explains two distinct methods for producing the skirt portion, referred to as “group name,” highlighting their advantages, challenges, and appropriate use cases. ### Method 1: Positioning Ball Arrangement and Simple Sewing - **Tools & Process**: - Use positioning ball tool with screen coordinate views (front/back/side/top) for accurate panel placement. - Panels are arranged in a closed simulation state to avoid conflicts. - Sew and simulate each panel independently to reduce computational load. - Suitable for medium-sized, simple group names. - Advantages: Simple, efficient, moves cohesively with garment pulls. - Disadvantages: Monotonous style, limited to medium-sized designs. ### Method 2: Adjusting Physical Properties for Stiffness - **Fabric Physical Properties Setup**: - Create a new fabric and edit physical properties via property editor. - Key parameters: - **Bending Strength**: Controls fabric hardness; higher values = harder to bend. - **Strength of Deformation**: Controls fold stiffness; higher values = less fold bending. - **Stretch**: Controls fabric stretchiness; lower values = harder to stretch. - Set bending strength to 0 (max hardness), deformation strength to 100 for firmness, and stretch to 30 for moderate elasticity. - **Simulation and Effect**: - Fabric behaves like stiff paper, producing stable, static structural effects. - Simulation speed slower due to fabric rigidity. - Suitable for static, structural designs or very large, scattered group names. - **Additional Tips**: - A clever method shared by a Shenzhen student involved using very large particle diameters (~500) to prevent bending, supporting the group structure effectively. --- ## Creating and Extending Outer Layers and Panels This section describes building the outer layer of the wedding dress, including panel extension, freezing layers, and sewing techniques to achieve a smooth simulation. - **Rectangular Plate Construction**: - Build rectangular plates for front waist and other areas, adjusting length visually. - Use two extension tools: extension plate line (uniform extension) and extension plate point (localized extension). - **Panel Arrangement and Simulation**: - Position panels close to seams but avoid overlapping to prevent simulation instability. - Freeze layers before simulation to improve performance. - Use hardeners in panels to reduce load and creases.

outer layers > 0) to manage multi-layer simulation. --- ## Designing and Simulating Decorative Elements (“Living Person”) This section explains designing decorative elements such as the “living person” (living design effects or pleats), using extension tools, curve editing, and simulation stabilizing methods. - **Building Decorative Panels**: - Create rectangular plates (e.g., height 50 cm) and extend them using extension board point tool. - Add 3-4 decorative elements as needed. - **Smoothing and Curving Lines**: - Convert straight lines to free lines to smooth decorative shapes. - Use editor tools to delete unnecessary lines and refine curves. - **Alignment and Level Setting**: - Adjust shape from multiple angles, ensuring no overlaps or floating lines that cause simulation issues. - Use fixing tools to shape curves and prevent backline penetration. - **Layering for High-End Effects**: - Add extra fabric layers such as lace or mesh on outer cross-sections. - Freeze base layers, add new frozen columns, and outer layers to improve simulation smoothness. --- ## Applying Fabrics, Textures, and Physical Properties This section details selecting and assigning fabric materials, textures, and physical attributes to different dress parts for realistic appearance and behavior. - **Fabric Selection**: - Use silk fabrics for the main body; organza for outer fabric; silk ribbon for upper body thin fabric. - Add multiple fabric types to the library for quick access. - **Layer Penetration Management**: - Adjust layer settings from inside to outside to prevent fabric penetration during simulation. - Inner layers have smaller penetration values;
